# Seeds whose SELF-HOST x86-64 result disagrees with the interpreter's, for
# TestDifferential_SelfHostX86_64 (internal/e2e/diff_oracle_selfhost_test.go).
#
# Format: <seed> <reason + issue>. Blank lines and # comments ignored.
#
# A row is a KNOWN COMPILER BUG being tolerated so the rest of the corpus keeps
# running — not a seed that is allowed to be wrong. The leg fails on a NEW
# divergence and equally on a LISTED seed that starts agreeing, so this list
# prunes itself as the bugs are fixed rather than becoming somewhere they are
# forgotten.
#
# For every row here the interpreter, native x86-64 and native arm64 agree with
# each other; that agreement is what says the self-host compiler is wrong rather
# than the generated program being invalid.
#
# Rows that have already left with their fix:
#   121 / 265 / 365    #6177, the maps runtime need-gate
#   228 / 455          #6207, a map literal with computed keys building itself
#                      string-keyed
#   4 / 20 / 28 / 29 / 48 / 52 / 99 / 117 / 123 / 241 / 324 / 362 / 364 /
#   375 / 482 / 502    #6188, an i64/u64 literal SUFFIX deciding the width
#
# That last batch was every "wrong values" row this file carried plus the
# arena-exhaustion one, and they shared a single cause: `infer_expr_width`
# classified a numeric literal by MAGNITUDE alone, so `979i64` read as 32-bit.
# fernsmith emits suffixed literals constantly, which is why one width rule
# accounted for most of the corpus's divergence — and why the note that used to
# sit here, "twelve of the fifteen have interp=0, worth checking as a group
# before reducing them one at a time", was pointing at the right thing.
#
# Seed 502 left differently, and the distinction is worth keeping: it no longer
# COMPILES. Its small-magnitude i64 literals flow through the generic `pick` /
# `id` helpers, so classifying them correctly as wide now reaches the
# erased-wide path and its `__lam_22` bails ("module is not IR-eligible"). That
# is a coverage loss — but it replaced a SILENT WRONG ANSWER (163 where the
# interpreter said 0) with a refusal. The gap was always there; the 32-bit
# misreading is what hid it. Re-measured after the prune, the compile ratio
# stayed above the leg's 0.30 floor, so this cost one seed rather than a class.
#
# Measured 2026-08-06 over seeds 0..511 (the leg's default corpus), after #6188.

# CRASHES — the self-host-compiled binary dies by SIGSEGV where the interpreter
# returns a value. NOT one bug: seeds 228 and 455 were the map-literal key-kind
# mistyping (#6207) and left with its fix; these four survive that AND the width
# fix that took every wrong-value row, so they are a different cause (or causes)
# and want their own reduction. They are now the entire list, which makes them
# the obvious next target on #6178.
59 SIGSEGV (self-host 139, interp 41) — https://github.com/JakeChampion/lang/issues/6178
97 SIGSEGV (self-host 139, interp 230) — https://github.com/JakeChampion/lang/issues/6178
144 SIGSEGV (self-host 139, interp 96) — https://github.com/JakeChampion/lang/issues/6178
200 SIGSEGV (self-host 139, interp 0) — https://github.com/JakeChampion/lang/issues/6178
